metadata.title: Check the Spec, Not the Vibe.
metadata.subtitle: The Brand Voice Enforcement Skill
metadata.purpose: Answer one real question in the Plain register: when Claude runs a brand-voice-enforcement skill, does it already know what a brand should sound like, or is it checking a draft against a file that spells the rules out? Lands the carry-out that the skill doesn't know your brand's voice — it checks writing against whatever its SKILL.md actually lists, and the limit is exactly what the file says.

beats.narration_text: Someone assumed Claude just knows their brand's voice from training. It doesn't — it checks against a written spec. So: does Claude already check my brand's voice?

beats.narration_text: A skill is a folder Claude reads before it works. This one is brand-voice-enforcement. Its SKILL.md file holds the full instruction set, in plain language — no hidden logic. Claude reads it, then acts. The file is the program.
The instructions are laid out in a Steps section. Claude reads each step in order and runs it — linear, no branching unless a step says otherwise.

production_viz.label: STEPS, IN ORDER
production_viz.caption: linear — no branching unless a step says so

beats.narration_text: Here's the actual job: check a piece of writing against whatever rules the SKILL.md lists — banned words, preferred phrasing, tone, whatever it actually says — and flag anything that doesn't match. Same file, same rules, every single run.

production_viz.label: CHECK, DON'T GUESS
production_viz.caption: only what the file lists gets caught

beats.narration_text: brand-voice-enforcement doesn't know your brand's voice — it checks your writing against whatever its SKILL.md actually lists. Same input, same output, every time. The limit is exactly what the file says, nothing more.

props.quote: brand-voice-enforcement doesn't know your brand's voice — it checks your writing against whatever its SKILL.md actually lists. Same input, same output, every time.
props.sparkLine: Check the file. Not the vibe.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Paste this into Claude: My brand voice rules are — no contractions, no exclamation points, always say customers, never users. Check this paragraph against exactly those three rules and tell me which line breaks which one. Don't flag anything outside that list. That's the same discipline the skill runs on: check only what's written down, nothing else.
